title: Geometric Mode-Selection Scores for Delay-Coordinates Dynamic Mode Decomposition
summary: Delay-coordinates dynamic mode decomposition (DC-DMD) is widely used to extract coherent spatiotemporal modes from high-dimensional time series. A central challenge is distinguishing dynamically meaningful modes from spurious modes induced by noise and order overestimation. We frame this as a mode-selection scoring problem: each mode receives a score that ranks it as true or spurious; any hard selection (threshold or clustering) is a downstream choice.
